course_outline_concepts: Per-slice vs per-task metrics: why aggregate numbers hide the interesting story
Comparing checkpoints: signed vs unsigned per-slice deltas, when a regression is real
Building a failure-ledger: what each known-failure-bucket looks like across training runs
The 'three-line chart vs 50-slice report' rule: pick based on decision being made

sources.what_to_extract: Per-capability synthetic pipelines (code, math, multilingual, reasoning, long-context, tool use, factuality); six-round iterative regime implies per-round per-capability regression detection; RM-gated rejection sampling separates SFT pool by capability; margin labels ('significantly better', 'better', 'slightly better') are the slice-level signal that justifies re-training RM each round.

Stage-specific attribution (SFT -> DPO -> RLVR gain per benchmark per size); RLVR lifts GSM8K/MATH while DPO lifts IFEval — this is the canonical per-stage per-slice ledger; architectural-stability ablation table enumerates spike-free fraction per trick.

Model-flow-as-artifact view: pretraining / mid-training / long-context / SFT / DPO / RLVR as labeled stages whose per-capability contribution can be audited; Base / Think / Instruct / RL-Zero branches from same base make slice deltas diagnostic of stage rather than confound.

Three-stage per-stage per-verifier ledger: +5-10pp on GSM8K, +~4pp on IFEval, neutral-to-positive on other evals from RLVR; 939K SFT prompts broken by source (57% public, 43% in-house synthetic); safety-specific DPO slice; per-mixture ablation methodology.

21 tasks x 6 categories (single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot, synthetic, code) — canonical per-task-category slicing; some tasks solvable at 4K (NarrativeQA) while real long-context signal concentrated in multi-doc QA / synthesis; task-quality variance is the argument for never aggregating.

13-task suite chosen after correlation study to cover distinct failure modes not redundant variants; knobs that define slice axes (length, distractor density, output cardinality, tracing hops, aggregation burden); effective context size metric; one-number-per-model is misleading since S-NIAH saturates while MK-NIAH / VT / CWE reveal the real ceiling.

Multi-category scoring (simple, multiple, parallel, parallel-multiple, relevance-detection, chat, Java/JS) — canonical failure-bucket table; AST matcher produces confusion-matrix-like (name-mismatch vs arg-mismatch vs call-when-irrelevant); pass^k for agentic consistency slices run variance from capability.

Knowledge-capacity framing: per-capability slicing more informative than loss-or-benchmark aggregate; controlled factual-tuple settings motivate the per-capability-storage-and-retrieval slicing that BFCL/RULER/LongBench later operationalize on natural evals.

Extrapolative vs contextual generalization distinction — two different slice axes that conflate in aggregate; RL only helps at edge of competence so per-difficulty-bucket slicing shows whether gain is real capability or easy-task reshaping; process-reward vs outcome-reward changes the *shape* of the failure distribution not only its mean.

'Review the 10 worst validation examples — they reveal systematic errors' — literal root of failure bucketing; 'neural net training fails silently' — per-slice regression surfaces what aggregate hides; 'predict-outcome-before-run' — attested regression-direction predictions become the signed-delta threshold the chapter codifies.

deliverables: figures/slice-report.html (self-contained mock eval report with per-slice bars, toggle aggregate vs per-slice view, failure-bucket table, ~200-280 lines)
hard_rules: No external CDN references in HTML (inline CSS/JS only)
Cite attested per-slice numbers from raw-data model reports; label inferred defaults
Tie the 'three-line chart vs 50-slice report' rule to a specific decision (go/no-go vs regression-triage) rather than to style preference
Ledger examples must be named failure buckets attested by at least one of the ten raw-data sources
